title: Paraneoplastic limbic encephalitis as a cause of new onset of seizures in a patient with non-small cell lung carcinoma: a case report
case_prompt: A 64-year-old man with a 60-pack-year smoking history was diagnosed with stage IV undifferentiated large-cell lung carcinoma after bronchial biopsy. Initial brain CT showed an edematous, non–contrast-enhancing area in the left temporal lobe, but he had no neurologic symptoms and declined MRI. He underwent four cycles of carboplatin, etoposide, and epirubicin, with a 50% reduction in the primary lung mass and mediastinal lymphadenopathy after three cycles. Twenty days after the fourth cycle, he was admitted for self-limiting complex partial seizures manifesting as motionless staring and facial twitching without secondary generalization. Relatives reported a two-week history of short-term memory loss, temporary confusion, anxiety, and depression. Treatment with levetiracetam and alprazolam was initiated. Brain MRI demonstrated findings of cerebral gliomatosis, and magnetic resonance spectroscopy supported this interpretation. Clinical and laboratory evaluations were not indicative of metabolic, infectious, vascular, drug-induced, or chemotherapy-related disease. Serum testing for anti-Hu antibodies was negative. A stereotactic brain biopsy revealed lymphocytic infiltration and gliosis without evidence of tumor cells.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Intracranial metastasis was considered but excluded because “the pathology specimen revealed brain tissue with areas of lymphocyte infiltration and gliosis, with no evidence of tumor cells.”  
2. Chemotherapy-related or drug-induced toxicity was considered and ruled out since “clinical and laboratory examinations were not indicative of … drug-induced or chemotherapy-related disease.”  
3. Infectious encephalitis was entertained but excluded because “clinical and laboratory examinations were not indicative of … infectious … disease.”  
4. Metabolic encephalopathy was considered and dismissed as “clinical and laboratory examinations were not indicative of metabolic … disease.”  
5. Vascular causes (ischemia or hemorrhage) were evaluated but ruled out since “clinical and laboratory examinations were not indicative of … vascular … disease.”  
6. Cerebral gliomatosis was suggested by imaging—“brain MRI … showed findings of cerebral gliomatosis” and “magnetic resonance spectroscopy … revealed findings of cerebral gliomatosis”—but was excluded by biopsy confirming inflammatory changes and “no evidence of tumor cells.”
